study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

nm2_1_modeling_method.detail: Two hierarchical Bayesian normative models: a hierarchical Bayesian linear model with site modeled as a random effect (HBLM) and a hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian process model adding a GP term for non-linear age effects (HBGPM); comparison/pipeline also fit a simple Bayesian linear model without site after harmonizing data via site regression, ComBat, or modified ComBat (and on raw data).
nm2_1_modeling_method.supporting_text: "we developed and compared two versions of a hierarchical Bayesian models that include site as a predictor. In a hierarchical linear version of the model, site is modeled hierarchically, resulting in a random effect for site ('Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model, HBLM'). In a non-linear version of the model, a Gaussian Process for age is added... ('Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model, HBGPM')." ... "then a simple Bayesian linear algorithm, with an additive term for age and sex, but without site as a predictor is used to make predictions in Stan"

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness from 34 bilateral Desikan-Killiany regions (left/right averaged) plus average cortical thickness across all 34 regions derived from FreeSurfer outputs.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: "we focused on cortical thickness measures of the 34 bilateral regions (averaged between left and right hemisphere) of the Desikian Killiany atlas parcellation ... and the average cortical thickness across all 34 regions. We chose to include only cortical thickness measures"
